name: Rishibha Biyani
feedback: The draft editor, readiness feedback, and feed preview form a clear workflow, and a generated draft survived reload. Tighten the generation so it uses the supplied facts without adding generic claims, and reconcile the inconsistent streak counts across screens.
tested: Create, Dashboard, History, Schedule; generated synthetic library-tracker draft; reload retained input and output.
limitations: No posting or seeded records changed.

name: Himanshee Ahluwalia
feedback: The editorial typography and table concept give this a distinctive identity, and selecting an evening updates checkout and seat totals. The February/March dates need a current availability model, and the reservation/payment completion remains unverified; add clear live-versus-demo labeling and persistent selection.
tested: Viewed process, tables, seating chart, menu, founder note, testimonials, application and checkout; selected first table, two seats, UPI; reload.
limitations: No application, booking, contact details, or payment submitted.

name: Shrividya Ramesh
feedback: The sports arenas, staged clues, and answer reveal make a playable quiz, and the completed round persisted. Make the IQ calculation and navigation consistent: a correct answer awarded 35 points while IQ fell from 60 to 53, and the surrounding statistics updated only after reload.
tested: Cricket clue unlock and correct Kane Williamson guess; result and reload persistence; IQ Matrix, Leaderboards, Friend Duels attempted.
limitations: No sharing performed.

name: Uttiya Biswas
feedback: The wellness onboarding has a calm visual hierarchy and an explicit demo entry. Native cycle-date entry could not be completed through the review tool, so the tracking features remain unverified; provide a skip path or preconfigured demo for assessment.
tested: Demo credentials entry, sign in, fictional first-name onboarding, date step and reload.
limitations: Review-tool limitation at native date input; core wellness screens inaccessible beyond onboarding. No real health data used.

name: Abhinav Dua
feedback: The compact dashboard, supplement stack, and bloodwork views are coherent and readable, and the built-in advisor prompt produces a response. Make demo assumptions explicit throughout, reconcile 0/3 taken with “All taken today,” and retain advisor history after reload before presenting this as a dependable tracker.
tested: Home, AI Advisor built-in example, My Stack, Progress, Profile, Bloodwork, reload.
limitations: No real health data, uploads, subscriptions, or seeded record changes; medical accuracy not assessed.

name: Kritika Garg
feedback: The daily cleaning dashboard has clear counts and staff availability. Schedule, Maids, Rooms, and Settings all returned 404, so implement those routes and a complete assignment flow before adding more dashboard polish.
tested: Today loaded, previous-day control, reload; all four main navigation destinations returned 404.
limitations: Existing staff availability was not changed.

name: Arnav Singh Negi
feedback: The large card target and immediate rule reveal make the basic game easy to use. Add deck progress, history, and resume behavior: the tested draws changed cards, but reload returned to the start and the experience remains a very small single-screen implementation.
tested: Two card draws, rule changes, reload reset, New Game.
limitations: No real drinking or external actions.

name: Shawn Jason
feedback: The restrained dashboard and evidence-based explanation make the social follow-up concept clear; the fictional chat correctly produced a promise-debt result. Preserve new analyses across reload and offer a clear path to save or resolve them, rather than leaving useful output on a temporary screen.
tested: Dashboard, seeded detail read-only, synthetic conversation analysis correctly identified promised book list, Generate Reply, reload.
limitations: No messages or uploads; existing debt records unchanged.

name: Sahira
feedback: The local demo exposes a complete reflection-to-dashboard workflow, and the new entry survived reload. Ground the pattern claims in actual entries: the fresh fictional library input was described as occurring in two recent entries, while the timeline also shows milestones beyond the 14-day demo.
tested: Local demo entry; Dashboard, Weekly, Timeline, Settings, Reflect; analyzed and saved fictional reflection; reload.
limitations: Local demo only; no real personal reflections. Saved synthetic reflection replaced the current day sample entry.

name: Vansh Arora
feedback: The paper-chit styling and role explanations fit the game well, and room creation produced a lobby and code. Provide a single-device demo or bot mode; additional tabs shared one identity in this review, so role dealing, guessing, and scoring could not be verified end to end.
tested: Created demo room AJ3RD, inspected lobby and leaderboard, attempted additional demo players in own tabs, reload.
limitations: Shared browser identity prevented four independent players; full round unverified.

name: Giaa Madan
feedback: The submitted link opens an AI Studio terms-acceptance gate, so the app itself could not be observed. Publish a directly accessible demo and restore access to the supporting brief; no visual or functionality score can be justified from this gate.
tested: Opened supplied URL; supporting Drive brief returned file not found.
limitations: Terms not accepted; app unobservable.

name: Raghav Dua
feedback: The Japanese vending-alley theme carries through machines, collection, and arcade with a convincing game economy. A capsule pull deducted 200 virtual coins and added an item that survived reload; improve low-contrast copy and reconcile the landing-page “eight machines” claim with the 15-machine interface.
tested: Alley, Arcade, Collection, Charm Capsule pull, collection/reload persistence.
limitations: Virtual coins only; other arcade games and later rank-locked machines not exhaustively played.

name: Riddhi Singla
feedback: The login screen has a clean fashion-oriented identity and the initial empty wardrobe message explains the concept. Authentication then blocked the wardrobe workflow; provide a reviewer login or guest wardrobe so outfit generation and saving can be assessed.
tested: Supplied /home briefly displayed empty wardrobe, then redirected to login.
limitations: Authentication required; no account created, no photos uploaded.

name: Gunjan Samdani
feedback: The warm mobile layout and food-based discovery concept are clear, with consistent Home, Explore, Chats, Plans, and Profile screens. Much of the core experience remains a mock: the search is displayed as static text and conversations/plans are prefilled; implement a real search-to-plan flow and label demo social/safety claims.
tested: All main navigation, People/Clubs tabs, attempted search, reload.
limitations: No invitations, messages, reviews, bookings, or seeded-plan changes.

name: Pranav Verma
feedback: The bracket interface and consistent ranking/profile screens make the interaction easy to understand. Clarify the scoring model—one professor showed 1,247 crowns but only six votes—and provide a sandbox vote flow so ranking updates can be tested without altering real faculty feedback.
tested: Vote screen, Ranking, Business, locked Admin, professor review detail, reload.
limitations: No faculty votes, reviews, demo requests, or roster edits submitted; write persistence unverified.

name: Tanmay Negi
feedback: The bot lobby, timed turns, card actions, and property-table updates demonstrate a substantial playable core. Improve session recovery and make game progress easier to read at a glance; the dense table and multiple action surfaces need careful treatment on smaller screens.
tested: Rules, quick play bots, game start, Pennsylvania Railroad placed, end turn, bot state, reload.
limitations: Full victory and independent multiplayer not tested; no chat messages.

name: Saksham Tandon
feedback: The flag library, daily challenge, and varied quiz modes form a focused learning product, with unusually clear caveats about incomplete catalogue data. The daily Hungary guess worked; finish the missing flag imagery and make anonymous history limits clear so users understand what reload preserves.
tested: Home, Explore, Daily correct Hungary guess, Quiz setup, Record Attempt setup, Facts, About, reload.
limitations: No Google sign-in; full 195-flag record and every quiz mode not completed.

name: Harish S Kumar
feedback: The animal artwork and simple runner controls connect well to the conservation learning cards. A run reached 63 metres, produced species-specific learning content, and retained the best score; deepen the challenge variety and make conservation sources more directly traceable.
tested: Home, How to Play/Learn, animal selection, Bengal Tiger start/jump/run end, conservation card, reload best score.
limitations: One animal played; no donations or external organization actions.

name: Ashish Lalwani
feedback: The broad agency workspace is visually consistent and the client search filters correctly across a detailed operational model. The AI output ignored the bookshelf instruction and returned generic fitness reels; prioritize reliable, persistent end-to-end workflows and distinguish working integrations from seeded demonstrations.
tested: All 15 sidebar modules; task form opened/cancelled; client search; synthetic AI generation; reload.
limitations: No task assignments, invoices, publishing, uploads, external integrations, or seeded-data changes.

name: Tamanna Khemani
feedback: The buyer-versus-influencer concept is well explained, and the sample produced a detailed customer chain that survived reload. Improve the long loading state and ground strong claims about grandparent spending in evidence; the output sensibly labels scores as AI estimates but some market conclusions sound more certain than the input supports.
tested: Landing, sample toy input, completed customer-chain analysis after roughly one minute, reload retained full report.
limitations: One sample tested; no claim of external market validation.

name: Vanshika Agarwal
feedback: The warm expense dashboard has a clear visual hierarchy and a useful manual-entry concept. Stats, Ask AI and Profile return 404, and the submitted demo expense never appears in activity or history after reload. Connect those routes and reconcile the conflicting transaction amounts before presenting the figures as a working tracker.
tested: Onboarding/manual tracking, Home, History, Stats, Ask AI, Profile, synthetic ₹10 expense submission and reload.
limitations: No bank connection or real financial data used.

name: Akanksha Srivastava
feedback: The gentle palette and three-step introduction explain the small-wins concept clearly. The next screen requires sign-in with no guest path, so logging, recaps and weekly progress could not be assessed; provide a reviewable demo account or guest mode.
tested: Landing screenshot and Let’s Go → sign-in. Brief connector returned 404.
limitations: No credentials provided; account creation not attempted. Core unobservable.

name: Twinkle Monga
feedback: The playful handwritten styling and contribution breakdown make the shared-jar idea immediately understandable. Synthetic partner names persisted, but the main flow then required UPI setup and the contribution pages retain canned character-specific copy; add a clearly nonpayment demo and make all partner text consistent.
tested: Setup with synthetic names, both partner contribution routes, Rules, reload persistence.
limitations: Stopped at UPI entry; no payments, agreement signing or fines initiated.

name: Vanshika Maurya
feedback: The mobile discovery layout and live text filtering make nearby-place browsing easy. Saving a place did not create a traceable new item in the collections, and dated July events are labelled this week; complete saved-state feedback and replace sample dates, reviews and contact details before treating this as a live campus directory.
tested: Home, Explore, search quiet yielding one result, place detail, Save, Saved reload, Events and Profile.
limitations: No calls, directions, reviews or RSVPs submitted; saving did not establish a traceable new collection item.

name: Aadish Soni
feedback: Circle provides a focused relationship-tracking workflow with useful cadence status and an uncluttered contact form. A synthetic contact and its note survived reload and list search filtered correctly; clarify whether the passwordless private-vault claim is a local demo or protected account before storing real contacts.
tested: Sample Email entry, Dashboard, Add Contact, synthetic contact and note, detail timeline, reload and All Contacts search.
limitations: No real contact data or messages. Account isolation and cross-device storage not verified.

name: Anushree Mukherjee
feedback: The notebook cover and serif typography give this habit journal a coherent identity. The dated daily page has no writing field and checkbox interaction produced no visible completion; Finish resets the timer, but the monthly spread and progress still read as samples. Connect daily entries, timer results and reload-persistent progress into one usable workflow.
tested: Cover, daily Journal, checkbox, History, Menu, Monthly Spread, Progress, timer Start/Pause/Finish, reload.
limitations: No real journal content entered.

name: Ankit Singhal
feedback: Hisaab translates household billing into useful category-specific forms, a monthly grid and a settlement breakdown. A synthetic vendor survived reload and appeared in every relevant view; improve the low-contrast warning banner and explain when default daily quantities become payable so the balance is auditable without relying on the zero-dispute claim.
tested: Today Journal, new synthetic newspaper vendor, Month Grid, Settlement Hub and reload.
limitations: Existing vendor records unchanged; no WhatsApp slips, payments or mass confirmation. Complex rate-history calculations not exhaustively verified.

name: Sameeksha Nigam
feedback: The directory, help requests and skill-focused profiles form a credible campus-network concept with consistent navigation. tested: Home, Discover shortcut and keyword searches, MU Hunt, Network, Profile, Ask MU and reload.

name: Shell Sheth
feedback: The eyewear imagery, restrained palette and typography create a distinctive retail presentation. tested: Collection, Craft, Story, Try on, Square shape recommendation, Surya selection and reload.

feedback: The bold visual hierarchy explains the quiz-to-bill-split journey clearly and correctly states that the app does not move money. Sign-in is required before the quiz, so the persona logic and split calculations could not be verified; provide guest access and show why each weighting is fair to the group.

name: Utkarsh Garg
feedback: The shipper landing page and itemised fare panel make the intended workflow clear. The Fleet Dashboard returns 404, and the demo quote shows Delhi–Jaipur as 1,023 km; replace simulated routing with validated distances and make the prominent live-network claims visibly consistent with the demo disclaimer.
tested: Home, quote form with Delhi/Jaipur and one-ton Mini Truck, price update, Fleet Dashboard, booking page revisit.
limitations: No booking confirmed, account created or payment; quote fields reset on revisit.

name: Guruprasad Shetty
feedback: The tenant, landlord and consent screens communicate a substantial rental-history concept, and the simulator correctly deducts 60 points for a dispute flag. Save Projection reports success but does not show the target on the dashboard and resets after reload; complete that persistence path and label unsupported verification, accuracy and deposit-waiver claims as illustrative.
tested: Landing, Tenant Portal, Landlord View, Consent & Tasks, simulator dispute toggle/save/reload, Tenancies, Landlord Reports and Help Center.
limitations: No real tenancy data, consent grants, application decisions or document uploads.

name: Bhagyam Maheshwary
feedback: The urgency ordering and compact summary make the food-waste problem easy to understand. Native date entry could not be completed through the review tool, so adding food, consumption and saved totals remain unverified; a sample-item demo would allow the full workflow to be assessed.
tested: Dashboard, Add Food synthetic name/date, retry with blur, validation response and reload.
limitations: Review-tool limitation: native date fill changed the visible value without the application accepting it. Existing foods untouched; core save/consume/persistence unobservable.

name: Binit Halan
feedback: The editorial visual style and searchable 101-case library support a clear interview-practice proposition. Search narrowed to the intended case, but saving and starting require member sign-in, so the interviewer and scorecards remain unverified; provide guest practice and consolidate duplicate section labels such as Market Entry and Market entry.
tested: Landing, library, margin search, Save case, Start case auth gate, Your progress; brief connector 404.
limitations: No credentials/account creation. Core interview and scorecard unobservable.

name: Kedar Kashid
feedback: The knowledge map, mistake explanations and subject-level study planning form a strong learning concept. The tested Carnot drill used a generic conservation question, and a short pasted note remained processing; prioritise grounded question quality and reliable source processing. Full-session progress persistence remains unverified because the five-question session was not completed.
tested: Recovered app from submitted document; Dashboard, Knowledge Map, Study Sessions, Flashcards, Mistakes Bank, Analytics, Study Materials, one drill answer, reload, synthetic note processing.
limitations: Author document acknowledges adaptive features and source upload WIP. Full five-question session not completed; material processing did not finish during review.

name: Navneet Kumar
feedback: The focused landing page explains equal/custom splits and adjustable reminder tone clearly. Account creation is required before the ledger or reminders can be inspected, so provide a guest demo with fictional debts and reviewable reminder drafts.
tested: Landing and Get started→account gate; brief connector 404.
limitations: No account, reminders, payment links or real contacts entered. Core unobservable.

name: Masoom Agarwal
feedback: The restrained research interface explains business classification, management credibility and source traceability clearly. Both analysis and report access lead to sign-in, so the research output cannot yet be graded; supply a guest report with working citations and a runnable ticker example.
tested: Lovable preview loaded, rendered app opened, Analyze a stock and View reports sign-in gates; brief connector 404.
limitations: No account creation or investment action. Core analytical quality unobservable.

name: Manvi Narang
feedback: The single-device handoff screens and clear role instructions make Mafia Night usable for an in-person group. Five-player assignment and a full night action sequence worked, including identifying the Mafia; add session recovery and clearer safeguards around accidental taps before relying on one device for a long game.
tested: Rules, five synthetic players, all role reveals, Mafia target, Doctor protection flow, Detective correct identification, morning and reload.
limitations: No real participants. Full day vote and final win condition not exercised.

name: Rishi Porwal
feedback: The submitted URL resolves, but it displays only the hosting placeholder Your app will live here, including after reload. Publish the actual application and supply an accessible brief so its portfolio workflow can be reviewed.
tested: Opened URL, allowed loading, reload, screenshot; brief connector 404.
limitations: No student app interface observable.

name: Soham Verma
feedback: Large pictorial controls and Indian-language labels suit a driver-focused interface. The preset trip tap produced no visible route change, and the emergency page claims a call and location sharing without showing verified status; clearly separate demonstration guidance from operational safety features.
tested: Home, Assistant, Navigation, Trips, read-only emergency screen, Delhi–Lucknow preset and reload.
limitations: No microphone/location permission, calls or messages. Voice recognition, live guidance and emergency delivery unverified.

name: Rashi Arora
feedback: The submitted artifact link shows Page not found with a sign-in option, and the accompanying brief was not accessible. Share a public working app or review credentials so the concept, interface and core flow can be assessed.
tested: Submitted Claude artifact URL screenshot/DOM; brief connector 404.
limitations: Cannot distinguish private artifact from removed artifact; no app observable.

name: shashwat bajpai
feedback: The operational navigation and cost ledger address a concrete warehouse workflow with receipt, issue and transfer records. Import shows Not Found, and the dashboard inventory value is $210.25 while the visible remaining transfer is $210.00; explain that reconciliation and provide an isolated demo for validating stock mutations and FIFO costing.
tested: Dashboard, Warehouses, SKUs, Receive, Issue, Transfer, Ledger, Import, Apply Filters and reload.
limitations: Existing records and stock untouched; no safe isolated transaction environment was identified, so mutation/FIFO correctness remains unverified.

name: Kartikey Thussu
feedback: The arcade presentation, difficulty controls and reduced-motion option make the game easy to approach. Delivery timing, wickets and pause/resume respond, and sound/motion settings survive reload; fix the landing instruction overlap with the stadium lights and make hit timing clearer for first-time players.
tested: Easy difficulty, sound off, reduced motion, Play, early shot feedback, wicket progression, pause/resume and reload.
limitations: Timed browser review did not land a scoring shot; nonzero high-score persistence unverified.

name: Vasudha Jajodia
feedback: The soft colours and family activity cards create a welcoming shared-space concept, and the Wordle accepted HOUSE and updated the player result to two tries. Family Tree, Shared Album, Scrapbook and Settings all lead to the same home screen; implement those distinct workflows and persist game progress before expanding the sample feed.
tested: All six sidebar destinations, wake-up screen, Wordle typed and individual keyboard inputs, reload.
limitations: No family greetings, comments, invitations or shared progress sent.

name: Ayush Vaidya
feedback: The supplied artifact resolves to Page not found with a sign-in option, and its accompanying brief was unavailable. Provide a public working version or review credentials so the application can be assessed.
tested: Submitted Claude artifact load and screenshot; brief connector 404.
limitations: Cannot distinguish private from removed artifact; no app observable.

name: K Rhythm
feedback: The editorial luxury styling and four-step inspection flow are coherent, and the supplied Hermès preset produced a detailed report. The new 94% result did not appear in My Scans, while Official Certificate conflicts with the preliminary-only disclaimer; fix report persistence and keep confidence, provenance and certification language honest.
tested: Sample preset→item details→photos→review→94% report, My Scans, reload and Sign In screen.
limitations: Preset only; no personal photos, purchase, expert contact or real authentication claims validated.

name: Jahnavi Tiwari
feedback: The sample venture report has a useful breadth of strategy views, and a saved evidence item survives reload. Make each Verified Fact traceable to an actual source link and show truthful connection status: the Workspace hub claimed Live OAuth Connected before sign-in. Custom venture analysis and Google exports remain unverified behind authentication.
tested: Viewed landing screenshot, all eight sample-report sections, Workspace and Google Workspace hub; opened source-verification dossier; saved Samsara evidence and confirmed the saved item after reload; inspected sign-in form. Brief retrieval returned Drive 404.
limitations: Sample workflow only; no account, OAuth authorization, exports or custom venture analysis. Source claims were not externally verified.
